Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

In a recent development, "The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.

Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

It's not just PS5 players that are struggling, either; some Xbox Series X players have reported crashes too, with one saying the game sometimes crashes after just 15 minutes.

Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or said whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

Unfortunately, there's no firm fix just yet. PlayStation's support page describes CE-108255-1 simply as "an error occurred with the game/application”, and its only advice is to "try updating your game". Highlight GTA 6 on your home screen, press Options, and choose Check for Update.

Beyond that, you can try the following, which come from Sony's general crash advice:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

Recent findings suggest that if you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI. While on the surface it looks like just a funny gag poking at auteur culture (and one developer in particular), Tenebrae Lux is a surprisingly solid, short puzzle game that (if you’re not using this guide) may take you a few hours to get through.

But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it rapidly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help. I get you. Here’s as simple a walkthrough as I could manage for Tenebrae Lux:.

Sources indicate that you’ll start out on the shoreline. You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects. To start with, you’re going to want to head to the left side of the shore (assuming you’re facing the shore from the beach you start on) where there are multiple run-down shacks lit by massive bright lights.

According to recent reports, inside these shacks are three puzzles on gridded boards. On those grids, multiple pieces are placed with different 3D shapes atop: three-tiered tall ones, middling spiky ones, and flat ones with a tiny dot in the middle. The flat ones don’t move at all, the middle-sized spiky ones can slide across the board and clear the flat ones if they land next to them, and the three-tiered tall ones and middle-sized ones clear one another in the same fashion. Your goal is to clear all the pieces off the board.

You can do these puzzles in any order. One of them is easy and straightforward, but the other two require a little bit more thinking. You’ll have to use the fact that the flat pieces don’t move and cannot be cleared by the three-tiered pieces to set up the three-tiers so they and the mountain pieces can clear one another once all the flat ones are off the board.

The three main puzzles in this area should be fairly simple to do, though there are a couple of hidden ones you can optionally do that are more difficult. On at least one, you might need to set up your board so you have two three-tier pieces set up with a gap between them that a middle-sized piece can easily get into after clearing a flat one. See below:.

When I move that mountain-shaped piece to the left, it will take out itself and all three of those other tiles with it.

This puzzle will easily make you feel like you’re losing your mind, but I highly recommend trying to work it out for yourself first, if you can.

When you enter the room upstairs in the bunker, you enter a loop that will keep perpetuating each time you go through the door and up the stairs. The room will be almost identical each time you enter it, but for two things. The first will be the calendar, which will show the date as being one of six different dates, and the second will be one of the other objects in the room.

Your goal is to find a six-digit code and enter it into the phone, followed by the # sign, to proceed.

In order to get the code, you need to pay attention to what day it is, and what is different in the room on that date. If you keep going up the stairs over and over, the dates will eventually cycle back through, so if you miss one don’t worry, you can keep going to see it again. The dates are as follows: October 11, 14, 20, 23, 27, and 30. You won’t see the dates in any particular order, but you’ll need to put them in that order when you input the numbers for each date into the phone.

The numbers themselves, you get from finding what’s “different” in the room on a given date, and working out what number the difference corresponds to. There are ten possible differences, and your playthrough won’t have all these objects in the roomâit’s random each time, though consistent within a single playthrough of the puzzle. Here are the ten possible differences:.

Once you get the code right, exit upwards one last time and on you go.

Recent findings suggest that this one was waaaaay more confusing to me than it needed to be. The goal is to cross the bridge off to the left of the ruins. The bridge has multiple rows of weird symbols on it. You have to walk over the correct symbol in order to proceed. If you walk over the wrong one, a lamp will go out. If you do it wrong three times, you fail and the puzzle resets.

The trick to figuring out the correct symbols is in the ruins and the poem on the plaque just outside.

The ruins will contain the following items, which correspond to the following descriptors in each of the seven lines of the poem:.

The items will be scattered across the ruins. Also in the ruins you will find a bunch of weird, esoteric symbols glowing on the ruined archways above. These symbols correspond to the symbols on the bridge.

In a recent development, to solve this, you need to visit each of the items in the order they appear in the poem, and match the item with the symbol on the ruins that corresponds to it, then follow the symbols across the bridge in order (the direction they’re facing doesn’t matter). It can be a bit tricky to figure out which symbol goes with which item. The best way I can describe it is the symbol for each item is the one that’s over the doorway “entrance” to each item, so the one you have to pass under to reach it.

In a recent development, here’s a map to show you what I mean. Orange circles are places where the objects can appear, and green triangles are where symbols are. I’ve numbered them, but please don’t mistake the numbers for the correctÂ order of the objects: that’s going to be determined by the poem, and the poem’s order is random.

Also note that #1 below is on the ground, because the arch has collapsed.

Recent findings suggest that this can still be confusing, so let me walk you through what I got as an example. Here’s my poem:.

First up is moon, which for me was straight ahead through the first door.

Two days of rest notes nothing, so we move to the third line, which mentions forests. Here’s the tree:.

Third verse mentions gold, then earth, in order. My trophy was past the mark that had crumbled to the ground, and my earth was at the very start of the puzzle:.

This next line is a bit tricky, as it mentions both sun and moon. But there are only seven lines on the bridge, and the items are only used one time each. So we just focus on sun here. I didn’t get a good picture of my sundial, sorry!

In a recent development, the last two lines in order mentions fire first, then drinking, which is water. Here’s fire:.

Sources indicate that so I’d follow those symbols in order across the bridge. It may help to draw a map on a piece of scrap paper or in a notebook for this one so you don’t have to slowly walk back and forth over and over.

If you fail, the puzzle will fully reset itself, and you’ll have to look at a latest version of the poem and ruins and try again.

This bit is a little creepy and again confusing at first, but quite easy once you work it out. All you have to do is walk in the door that’s the furthest away from any of the figures walking through the doors.

In the photo above, the man is walking toward the third door from the right, so I want to go to the farthest door on the left.

Industry observers note that as you go, more figures will start to appear. When there are multiple, you want to try and split the distance as best as possible. You also have to avoid any doors that say they’re out of order, so if they have a sign on them, go to the next one furthest away from the man. On the last set of doors, there was no way to get away from the men, so I just walked directly between two of them.

Once you pass through the last door, you’ve officially beaten Tenebrae Lux!

If you were curious how accurate the utility towers in Grand Theft Auto 6 the answer appears to be: Very.

The best way to play is just to experience the game, even if most of us are too internet-pilled to do that.

People don't like having to scroll a big number back and forth to deposit a specific amount.

It's a funny ad poking fun at another substantial franchise, but is a bit awkward as Rockstar deals with its own employees trying to form a union.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

#97287. Industry News: The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2234 w)

Industry News: The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once noted.
  • Industry observers note that but three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there.
  • For centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once noted. And on Christmas Day, the royal family will be seen en masse during their annual walkabout on their way to services at St. Mary Magdalene Church on the Sandringham estate. For years, the holiday stroll, which features major and minor royals mingling with the public, has been a milestone event on the royal calendar.

Industry observers note that but three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there. While Andrew has disappeared into his newly introduced life at Marsh Farm in Norfolk, Harry and Meghan have continued the tradition of the walkabout, reportedly infuriating the palace with a planned meet-and-greet with a small group of well-wishers in Nottingham. Although no longer working members of the royal family, it seems the couple knows the value and the power of this famous tradition, whose origins are far more recent than many believe.

For centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament. The first Buckingham Palace balcony appearance was not until 1851, when Prince Albert came upon the idea of Queen Victoria appearing to celebrate the Great Exhibition of London.

Sources indicate that the leading figure behind the idea of making the monarchy more visible to the public was a surprising one: the dour, but savvy George V, who ascended the throne in 1910. “I may be uninspiring,” he admitted, “but I’m damned if I’m an alien.”.

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince William waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 16, 1990. Pictured: Prince Edward, Duchess Of York, Queen Mother, Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, Prince William, The Grand Duchess Josephine Charlotte Of Luxembourg, Prince Harry, Prince Charles, Lord Frederick Windsor, Princess Diana and Lady Rose Windsor.

These royal appearances ramped up significantly during the first World War, when the royal family came under scrutiny for their German lineage. George visited everyday soldiers on the Front, and Queen Mary and her children spent hours visiting the wounded in hospitals.

“George took ‘getting out and about’ to new levels. He visited industrial areas and poor housing, went down a coal mine and went on a relentless round of opening hospitals and inspecting regiments,” royal news website Royal Central notes. “Queen Mary once retorted to a princess complaining about yet another hospital visit: ‘We are the royal family—and we love hospitals.’”.

However, these events were still carefully curated, with a distance maintained between the royal family and those they were visiting. It was not until 1939, that the first unofficial walkabout occurred, when King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (better known as the Queen Mother) went to tour Canada on a goodwill tour in the midst of the looming war. In May, the couple laid a wreath at Ottawa National War Memorial while an estimated 10,000 veterans looked on.

In a recent development, overcome with emotion, the royal couple decided to go into the crowd to speak with onlookers. A CBC radio journalist watching the scene could hardly have sounded more in awe. “They all look most happy, most excited,” the reporter stated. “One had the hand of the queen in one hand and the hand of the king in another. A delighted expression.”.

Recent findings suggest that george and Elizabeth were equally touched, and continued these meet-and-greets throughout the tour. “I lost my heart to Canada and to Canadians, and my feelings have not changed with the passage of time,” the Queen Mother recalled.

According to recent reports, known for her effusive personality and warmth, the Queen Mother became a pro at speaking with everyday subjects. During World War II, George and Elizabeth were praised for going among the people in bombed out areas devastated by the Blitz, listening to their woes and offering encouragement and strength.

Queen Elizabeth II on walkabout in Launceston, Tasmania, during her tour of Australia, 1970.

But it was not until Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip toured Australia and Upcoming Zealand in 1970 that the modern walkabout was truly introduced into the British royal calendar. There are different origin stories about how the modern walkabout came to be. One version asserts that it was a spontaneous decision of the Queen to walk to her next stop in order to chat, shake hands and accept flowers from schoolchildren in New Zealand.

Others say that first walk was the brainchild of the modernizing Australian courtier William Heseltine, known as the “mastermind behind the monarchy.” A firm believer in making the family seem more approachable and normal, he was also behind the 1969 Royal Family documentary. But if that project proved to be controversial, the walkabout (a term coined as a result of the tour) was a smash hit.

According to Kitty Kelley, the first royal walkabout did not occur in London until 1972, during the celebration of Elizabeth and Philip’s 25th wedding anniversary. “People were agog; their sovereign had never been known to speak to ordinary people,” Kelley writes in The Royals. “This was the first royal walkabout London had ever seen, and flag-waving Britons cheered as the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, and Princess Anne melted into the crowd, greeting people and trying to make the royal family appear less remote.”.

Industry observers note that while the Queen reportedly enjoyed the intimacy of the walkabout, not every royal family member was quite as thrilled. “At nineteen years old suddenly being dropped in the middle of the street, suddenly being told to pick someone and talk to them,” Princess Anne stated. “Fun? No, I don’t think so. A challenge.”.

Queen Elizabeth II visits the Town Hall in Sydney with Emmet McDermott, Lord Mayor of Sydney, during her tour of Australia, May 1970.

Industry observers note that soon, the walkabout was a major part of every royal’s schedule, and family members had to learn how to do them—like it or not. “I learnt the way a monkey learns—by watching its parents,” King Charles once said.

Recent findings suggest that during international tours, the walkabouts made a packed schedule even more tiring, but Queen Elizabeth II never faltered. “On a tour of Canada, visiting Saskatchewan, the Canadian minister Alvin Hamilton was concerned that the Queen had been on her feet all day and had not even requested a ‘health break,’” Karen Dolby writes in The Wicked Wit of Queen Elizabeth II. “Her private secretary breezily replied that the Minister for Northern Affairs and National Resources need not worry, ‘Her Majesty is trained for eight hours.’ It’s impossible not to wonder about the training sessions.”.

In a recent development, she also leaned upon her sense of humor when meeting folks of all different stripes. “On a walkabout in Scotland, a helpful observer commented that she looked just like the Queen, to which she quickly replied, ‘How reassuring,’” Dolby notes.

According to Dolby, the Queen also developed a system to communicate with her staff while talking with the public. If things were going well, she held her handbag in the crook of her left arm. If she wanted someone to relieve her so she could move on, the handbag was dropped to her side.

It has been revealed that but the person who truly transformed the modern walkabout was Princess Diana, much to her husband Prince Charles’s chagrin. “Charles was smart enough to see what a stunning political asset Diana had become—but he was also deeply disturbed by all the adoration coming his young wife’s way,” Tina Brown writes in The Diana Chronicles.

Industry observers note that from the start it was clear the young Princess had a connection with everyday people unlike any other royal. During a walkabout while touring Wales in 1981, Charles joked, “I seem to do nothing but collect flowers these days, I know my role.”.

It has been revealed that as Dianamania swept the world, the Princess became more and more comfortable with connecting with her often-rabid fans. Far from a stiff gloved handshake, she would clasp hands gloveless, hug well-wishers, kneel to speak with children. Frustrated that Diana constantly pulled focus, Charles delivered pithy one-liners with a forced smile. At one walkabout, the crowd openly groaned when they realized Charles was coming to their side, not Diana. “It’s not fair is it?” Charles quipped to the crowd. “You’d better ask for your money back.”.

But despite Charles’s jealousy, he could not deny the impact Diana had during these walkabouts. “Everyone was really buoyed up to see her and she was making an effort to go along and speak to people and people appreciated the effort she put into meeting them,” one person she spoke with remembered. “I know it was her job but she gave that little bit extra to people that made her different and stand out.”.

Sources indicate that “She made people happy,” he noted. “It’s a rare gift.”.

In a recent development, catherine, Princess of Wales, has followed in her mother-in-law’s footsteps as a walkabout all-star. According to historian Robert Jobson, Catherine was initially scared during the walkabout, offering up the stiff refrain, “Thank you so much. We are so delighted to be here,” over and over. But she rapidly acclimated and has become known for her chatty and warm ways. “There’s a real art to walkabouts,” she has stated. “Everybody teases me in the family that I spend far too long chatting. I still have to learn a little bit more, and to pick up a few more tips, I suppose.”.

In a recent development, in fact, it has become a sport for the press to catch Prince William subtly attempting to move Catherine along, often eventually giving up. During the Christmas Day walkabout in 2024, she was the last royal to leave the receiving line, quipping “I think I’ve lost my family!”.

According to royal author Robert Hardman, King Charles can also be unusually chatty. No one quite wants to go up and go, ‘Sir, can you get a move on?’ he notes. “Instead, Queen Camilla will nudge him in the small of his back with the corner of her handbag.”.

In a recent development, but the predilection is one Camilla shares as well. On a walkabout in Wrexham, an irritated Charles was overheard telling an aide “Can we try to get [Camilla] back again? Please? We need to go! I was trying to wait for her, but she goes on!”.

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend University of the South Pacific on October 24, 2018 in Suva, Fiji.

According to recent reports, learning the art of the walkabout—what to say, what not to say—is a lesson every royal must figure out, often on the job. When Meghan Markle married Prince Harry in 2018, she admitted her ignorance. “I never saw pictures or videos of a walkabout,” she claimed.

In a recent development, and with the advent of cell phones, the job has become much more difficult. “I’m glad that I’m not starting now because at least you had people to talk to. Now you don’t really. Phones are bad enough, but the iPads—you can’t even see their heads,” Princess Anne mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that and these engagements can occasionally go south. In 2018, the Duchess of Sussex was rushed out of a market in Fiji after the walkabout got out of hand. There are also the occasional overzealous fans, including recently when a woman attempted to kiss Prince William on the cheek. And who can forget the supremely uncomfortable walkabout at Windsor after the Queen’s death in 2022, when a warring William, Catherine, Harry and Meghan greeted public mourners. It was, Catherine reportedly noted, “one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do.”.

Sources indicate that walkabouts are also a logistical headache for royal protection officers. “You are always aware of who is in the crowd,” former royal bodyguard Simon Morgan explained to Hello! “That is one of the positives of our royal family, they always want to go and meet people and as a protection officer, you have to accept what their wishes are. The current trend of hugs, high fives and selfies, that’s going to continue, so the protection officer’s job is really brought to the front then, because the protection officer is constantly looking for what could go wrong, you are constantly working things through your mind for the ‘what if, what if, what if.’.

But the walkabout reveals no sign of disappearing anytime soon. And come Christmas Day, there will be cheers, hugs, and an enormous amount of quick, polite chats about the weather that citizens who wait and brave the winter cold will never forget.

It has been revealed that “I’m praying for Jaylen,” his teammate Kevin Winston Jr. told reporters during an August press conference. “I talked to him about it, having went through the same thing. I told him he’s gonna be just fine. I know Jaylen as a person, I told him I’m praying for him and best of luck with everything. I talked to him even before anything happened, just wishing the best and make sure he’s keeping his head high.”.

I’m feeling that myself, so I’m excited for Jaylen and I’m praying for him, as well.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Phasmophobia's next patch, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.
  • Industry observers note that the headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School.
  • Sources indicate that the Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phasmophobia's next patch, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

Industry observers note that the headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

Sources indicate that the Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

According to recent reports, you'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and latest buttons let you quickly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," said Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive.".

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free update and will be available on all platforms.

Industry observers note that phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for problems with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

Tech Report: So Is The $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Actually Worth It?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (992 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics.
  • In GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall.
  • According to recent reports, first up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics. So, now that GTA 6 is here and I’ve spent over 150 hours with it, I can share what’s in the Ultimate Edition, how you access this stuff, and if it’s worth upgrading from the standard $80 version of GTA 6. The short version is…eh, probably not.

In GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall. These stores include an exclusive tattoo parlor, street clothing shop, and hair salon. Now, at first, I thought it was pretty shitty of Rockstar to hide stores behind a paywall. And to be clear, it still does suck that a few shops are only accessible if you pay $20 more. But after playing GTA 6, I discovered that the world is filled with over 600 stores. There are already so many clothing, car, hair, make-up, and nail options in the base game. So the Ultimate Edition’s extra few stores don’t feel that necessary. And after actually visiting these shops and seeing what they have to offer, I don’t think people are missing out on that much.

According to recent reports, first up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear. There’s some alright stuff in here, including some nice-looking jeans for Jason and a cool graphic shirt or two. And a really wild fuzzy hat for Lucia. But the options in here aren’t something you need to have. You can create plenty of great and cool outfits without stopping by this Ultimate Editionâonly retailer.

Next up is the tattoo shop Electric Fang. Of all the Ultimate Edition stores, this is the coolest one to enter. And I do think some of Electric Fang’s tat designs are solid. But again, there are so many other options in the game for ink that I’m not sure these are very necessary or worth the $20 upgrade.

It has been revealed that sara’s Unisex Salon might be the best of the bunch as it offers some stylish hairdos for both Jason and Lucia. But on top of that, it offers some really nice makeup options for Lucia and cool nail art, too. I ended up using some of these options during my time as Lucia because I liked them so much. Still, again, there are so many other good options for haircuts and nail art already in GTA 6 that I’m not sure you need to spend $20 more on this version.

Recent findings suggest that there are also two exclusive car mod garages in GTA 6‘s Ultimate Edition. One of them, Rideout Customs, offers some really gaudy and exotic paint and accessories options. If you wanted a neon-pink car with stripes painted to look like cheetah print, well, this is the place for you.

The other mod shop, One-Eyed Willie’s, is more useful. It offers up some really nice off-road options. There aren’t nearly as many off-road modding options in GTA 6 as there are for street cars, so losing out on access to this in the base game is a shame. I also love that One-Eyed Willie’s offers up a random paint job for every car in the game, including non-off-road vehicles, that you can only see once it’s applied. I brought my Banshee into the shop, and it received this pretty pink design that I loved.

The Ultimate Edition also includes some unique free clothing items based on characters from an in-universe cartoon you can watch. These clothes are fine. I guess if you like the show a lot, they might be fun to wear. But…eh.

According to recent reports, beyond the stores and cosmetics, there are some exclusive vehicles you get access to in the Ultimate Edition, but some of these are only available during chapter one for story reasons. The only thing from the Ultimate Edition I used regularly and still use often when I play is the Vapid off-road truck. It’s fast as heck, a great option for driving on the dirt, and can be upgraded into a beast that can hold a lot of stolen loot. There’s also a classic car scavenger hunt side mission hidden behind the paywall, but after 150 hours I’ve barely interacted with that thing.

It has been revealed that answering the massive question of “Is the Ultimate Edition worth it?” is tricky, because it depends entirely on what you value and your taste for fashion and cosmetics. I’ve provided some samples of what’s on offer and how it fits into the larger GTA 6 world.

My opinion is that if you can afford the extra $20, a few bits of the Ultimate Edition are nice and worth the upgrade. But for the most part, if you just want to play Grand Theft Auto 6 to enjoy the open world and its story, you don’t need this upgrade. You’ll have a great time with the base game and never think to yourself, “Boy, I wish there were 30 more shirts and a few more cars in this!” GTA 6 is already massive. Don’t worry about making it a bit bigger.

A Vice City mode was using music made by AI.

If you were curious how accurate the utility towers in Grand Theft Auto 6 the answer appears to be: Very.

The best way to play is just to experience the game, even if most of us are too internet-pilled to do that.

People don't like having to scroll a big number back and forth to deposit a specific amount.

It's a funny ad poking fun at another big franchise, but is a bit awkward as Rockstar deals with its own employees trying to form a union.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

On that note, when Vanity Fair editor Mark Guiducci was given the task of profiling the megastar, he had a bigger task than he initially thought. The interview has now gone viral for awkward reasons, but Guiducci is defending his work and sharing a complimentary note about Chalamet.

Industry observers note that while Guiducci is normally an editor at the aforementioned publication rather than a writer, Chalamet still personally requested for this profile to be written by him, and that feels like a pretty tall order. Because Chalamet can’t go to many places in public due to his celebrity status, Guiducci invited the star over to his own apartment. This was apparently done in the hope that if Guiducci opened his own life up to Chalamet, he would be more willing to reveal more about himself, as the editor himself told Page Six.

However, this turned out not to be the case. Chalamet remained incredibly guarded and opted out of talking about his life. He declined to answer questions or comment on his high profile relationship with Kylie Jenner (with the latter admittedly being something he's long opted not to discuss). He did however spend a lot of time making observations about Guiducci’s home decor, which ended up becoming the centerpiece of the article. As a result, the story has gone viral due to Chalamet's evasive, awkward nature as well as the piece feeling more like it's about Guiducci’s apartment rather than Chalamet.

Despite the criticism, the Vanity Fair editor is still defending his work and his subject. He may have not been an open book, but Guiducci still made sure to note how normal the Oscar nominee felt to be around, and despite him stocking his kitchen and fridge with anything Chalamet could potentially want to eat or drink, the actor was surprisingly very low maintenance. He stated:.

It has been revealed that he was a lovely houseguest, and a cheap date. He drank tap water. And he’s welcome back any time.

Sources indicate that considering Chalamet grew up in Upcoming York City himself and still spends a lot of time in the Substantial Apple, he’s likely used to drinking New York’s tap water. Plus, I wouldn't be surprised if he had some sort of awareness that if he asked for anything specific it would end up in the article. I personally don’t doubt that Chalamet was kind, charming, and easy going, especially since the Dune star has been described as being “normal” before. It’s just hard to get a true read on a person when the person in question is aware they’re being observed.

Industry observers note that what seems to strike people most about Chalamet's lack of commentary is how it runs in contrast to how open he seemed to be during last awards season. It was during that time that he was promoting his sports dramedy, Marty Supreme. Of course, it was also during that promotional run that he received backlash for his viral comment regarding ballet and opera. However, Chalamet was defended in some circles.

Right now, the Little Women alum is under the biggest microscope possible, and it makes sense that he would have his guard up. Maybe he’ll become less guarded as time goes on, and his status as one of the last movie stars doesn’t feel so fragile. We’ll just have to wait and see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, use of generative AI in game dev remains as contentious as it does ubiquitous—a recent GDC report found that around 40% of devs use AI, but more than half think its influence has been negative. Ubisoft is continuing to double down on the technology, this time with Motherbrain, a new subsidiary fashioned from the team behind its "first playable generative AI experience.".

As reported by VGC, Motherbrain's purpose is to develop "AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences … Its current focus is on fresh player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large scale systemic worlds," according to an earnings report which was released Thursday.

The information comes at a turbulent time for the publishing giant, which just laid off 166 employees even after Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced "outperformed expectations." A sweeping internal overhaul earlier this year saw the manufacturer reorganize its workforce into a throng of "creative houses," a decision which led to swathes of layoffs and six project cancellations, including the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake.

It's not clear what Motherbrain are at work on, in specific terms, right now, but there may be some clues in its past work. That playable AI "experience" I mentioned earlier is none other than Teammates, an R&D project based on a prior experiment with uncanny AI "neo-NPCs.".

According to recent reports, teammates aimed to allow players to command NPC squadmates in a rudimentary shooter game with a microphone, and using AI, have those squadmates react believably. It's not far off, at least conceptually, from what we've seen in games like Where Winds Meet and Fortnite, both of which have experimented with AI-powered NPCs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

The couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

The busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing.

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

While in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday.

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

Sources indicate that the highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble.

According to recent reports, since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

It marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, New Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

It was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

Latest Update: Unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has been rated in Korea

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).
  • As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't confirmed a Complete Edition for the game yet.
  • The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't confirmed a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming claims is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially declared.

If Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

Complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an update introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and new skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a upcoming high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

According to recent reports, I’ve played over 150 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. You might think I’ve seen it all, and that I know everything there is to know about the game. Nope! I’m still discovering new mechanics, features, and open-world moments after all this time. This includes some very handy control shortcuts I recently learned about that will make your life in Vice City a little easier.

Industry observers note that first off, let’s start with the whole reason I wanted to write this blog. Did you know that you can rapidly toggle your car radio on and off without having to enter a submenu? All you have to do is double-tap left on the D-pad, and Jason or Lucia will turn the radio on or off.

I had no idea you could do this until I saw people sharing it on Reddit. The game doesn’t explain this shortcut, as far as I can tell. I couldn’t even find it mentioned in the in-game help menu, which does include lots of other nifty tips and tricks.

Here’s another trick I just learned about: You can double-tap the circle/B button while in a car to cycle the headlights between off, high beams, and low beams.

In a recent development, I thought you had to hold left on the D-pad to open up the vehicle submenu to turn off the headlights, but nope! And again, this isn’t mentioned in the help menu and if a prompt appeared during the normal course of the game to explain this, I and many others must have missed it.

Here’s another useful thing you can do inside cars: If you double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving, you’ll exit the vehicle without turning off the engine or radio.

GTA 6‘s help menu does call this out and mentions you can do this at speed to have your car drive into something while you roll out the side to safely. But again, I can’t remember a single time when the game forced me to do this or taught me that it was possible. I learned from a random post online. I guess I should have dug through the help menu more, but come on, who is doing that in Grand Theft Auto?

Another feature mentioned in the help menu that I just learned about is the ability to click the right stick in and yell at nearby drivers. Rockstar refers to this as the road rage button, and it’s a good thing to have in a game where NPC drivers, inspired by real Floridian drivers, suck shit and drive like maniacs.

One more useful control trick: You can double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving a boat to get up and walk around the deck while the boat keeps on cruising.

According to recent reports, the next time I boot up GTA 6, I’m going to start double-tapping random buttons during different parts of the game to see what other hidden shortcuts and control options Rockstar has buried in this massive game. And if you want some more useful hidden features, check out this blog about how to flip cars and sit anywhere you want in GTA 6.Â.

The day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be debuted by a member of his own party.

According to recent reports, over a year into her tenure as CBS News’ Editor-in-Chief, Bari Weiss has sought to move the storied organization into a upcoming era. Those attempts have apparently come with some growing pains, however, as the network has seen staffing changes and fluctuating ratings in recent months. At the same time, drama has been swirling around Weiss due to her reported vision for the brand and editorial decisions she’s made. Now, the company is experiencing more major staffing shakeups months after those 60 Minutes exits.

Industry observers note that in the aftermath of the Paramount Skydance/Warner Bros. Discovery merger, the media conglomerate Skydance has been born, and further consolidation is on the horizon. The new company recently offered buyouts to employees at CBS News, and dozens of employees reportedly accepted the deals. Status (via The Daily Beast) reports that different departments within the Eye Network’s news branch were impacted, including CBS Evening News, CBS Mornings, 60 Minutes and the company’s news bureaus.

It has been revealed that A source spoke out about this major development, saying “It’s pretty much an extinction-level event.” That particular insider was apparently from the London bureau, which has reportedly been hit the hardest by the buyouts. As for the cause of this, it’s mentioned that London-based employees had been displeased with Foreign Editor Shayndi Raice since she allegedly called out staffers for “insubordination.” Concerns about CBS News being merged with (the recently acquired) CNN are also said to have factored into these staff exits.

How Bari Weiss Responded After Being Asked If She’d Like To Run CNN.

Sources indicate that what’s also notable about this situation is that it comes on the heels of a significant development regarding CBS News’ Face the Nation. Senior executive producer Mary Hager is leaving the show and the network after having worked there for 35 years. (It’s unclear whether Hager’s departure has to do with her accepting a buyout.) Additionally, executive producer Anne Hsu is leaving as well for a new gig with the network’s Hong Kong bureau. So Weiss now finds herself in the position to reshape the show after allegedly having considered firing host Margaret Brennan earlier this year.

It has been revealed that it’s also worth mentioning how this round of buyouts has apparently impacted 60 Minutes. Per the report, more than a half dozen employees opted to take buyouts, yet none of those were reportedly senior-level employees. Yet this marks yet another change at the manufacturer amid continued headlines about declining ratings in the aftermath of this summer’s staffing changes.

Recent findings suggest that weiss and 60 Minutes executive producer Nick Bilton made some major changes to the news magazine show on May 28, 2026 (which is allegedly known as “Black Thursday” within the company). On that day, the company officially parted ways with veteran correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega as well as EP Tanya Simon and others for reasons that have still yet to be specified. And, shortly after that, another seasoned correspondent – Scott Pelley – was fired after a heated meeting with Bilton. It was during that conversation that Pelley allegedly accused Weiss of “murdering” the show.

In a recent development, those high-profile firings aren’t the only controversies that have swirled around 60 in recent months. As has been the case with other CBS News programs as of late, the show has seen viewership numbers that have come in below the averages of the previous season. On top of that, some former staffers continue to criticize Weiss’ leadership, and they’ve made claims about editorial bias under her direction. Weiss and co. have denied claims of editorial interference, and some staffers have praised her approach to her job.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that still, Bari Weiss did recently address concerns regarding 60 Minutes, and she declared that the show had been doing “tremendously well.” There reportedly remain concerns, however, about what lies ahead for the show and CBS News as a whole. At this point, questions remain, especially amid these recent staffing shakeups due to the buyouts.

Trust in the face of a lifetime of conditioning is hard to come by, and allowing yourself to be vulnerable to something youâve been taught doesnât see you as a person feels downright impossible. Yet Fenris and Hawke find a way. â Kenneth Shepard.

In a recent development, despite the fantastical framing, Dorianâs love story in Dragon Age: Inquisition is one that too many queer people are familiar with. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

While families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other reveals mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Industry observers note that theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's tech giant town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

Sources indicate that A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the upcoming sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

According to recent reports, mobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he states he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates newly introduced maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Company all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

According to recent reports, best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other indicates on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

The great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Sources indicate that adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a upcoming adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6MoviesRed Dead Redemption 2Rockstar Games.

With many legacy franchises in decline and few new ones taking off, Hollywood has turned to video games for significant box office blockbusters. There have been huge success stories like Minecraft and big bombs like Borderlands. But some of the biggest video game series have yet to make the jump to the silvers screen. Chief among them is Grand Theft Auto. Could that be about to change?

It has been revealed that according to a report in The Ankler this week, the answer is no. Multiple sources told the outlet that Rockstar Games isn’t interested in doing a movie adaptation of GTA. It makes sense, in a way, since GTA has increasingly become a series about bringing prestige, cinematic storytelling to the messy, systems-driven gameplay of open-world gaming. Putting that engine in reverse would be a bit like turning the video game version of Indiana Jones back into a movie. Who would ever do that?

It has been revealed that but it sounds like Rockstar, owned by Take-Two, is interested in shopping around the rights for a movie or TV adaptation of its Western open-world series, Red Dead Redemption. The Ankler adds that a number of $100 million was at one point thrown around for the price of licensing Red Dead. It points out that Amazon paid $250 million for the TV rights to Lord of the Rings.

Red Dead is in a similar lane to The Last of Us, which HBO managed to thread the needle on making into a prestige television show that still hooked fans of the game. It’s easy to imagine a similarly placed streamer doing the same for Rockstar’s IP, with internal executives pointing to mood boards that include the critical success of things like Deadwood and the commercial appeal of things like Yellowstone.

âWeâre very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment weâre always proud of,â Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, who used to be COO at 20th Century Fox, said in an interview on The David Rubenstein Show November 12. âWe would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it. If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. Itâs a high bar to do that. And of course, thereâs always a risk of failure. So we donât rule it out, but weâre very, very selective.â.

He’d given shareholders a more detailed account of this reasoning back in 2023 during Hollywood’s Barbenheimer-craze”.

Recent findings suggest that the hit ratios in the motion picture business are vastly lower than they are in the interactive entertainment business. Our hit ratios for console properties are in the 80 percent or 90 percent. The hit ratio for a well-run movie studio is around 30 percent, which is to say there’s a 70 percent chance that the movie that we license could fail. And so in success, the number, in terms of the benefit to our bottom line…it’s not zero, but it’s not really material to what we do around here. And in failure, we run the risk of compromising the underlying intellectual property.

The race to adapt other popular game franchises is already well underway. According to The Ankler, Amazon, Netflix, and FX are paying between $15 million and $25 million per episode for adaptations of Tomb Raider, Assassin’s Creed, and Far Cry. Those are essentially mid-range Hollywood blockbuster budgets.

According to recent reports, but Take-Two hasn’t rushed to turn its IP into streaming adaptations, and following the disaster that was the Borderlands movie, which was in production prior to it acquiring series maker Gearbox Entertainment, it has good reason to be. It’s games are already breaking sales and revenue records that Hollywood can’t compete with (GTA 6‘s day-one revenue eclipsed Avengers: Endgame). Why jeopardize that for a small side deal? A good Red Dead show could help the game sell ten million more copies, but a bad one could severely hamper its growing popularity beyond traditional gaming audiences.

“They thought weâd be blinded by the lights and that just wasn’t the case,” Rockstar cofounder Dan Houser, who left to form his own entertainment company, remarked last year when talking about past discussions. “We had what we considered to be multi billion dollar IP, and the economics never made sense. The risk never made sense. In those days, the perception was that games made poor-quality movies.”.

A 2008 adaptation of Max Payne, which Remedy Entertainment developed but Rockstar publishes, starred Mark Wahlberg and was moderately successful at the box office but critically panned with a 15 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. The misstep didn’t doom the series, which eventually got Max Payne 3 and is currently slated for remakes of the first two games, but it’s clearly not the sort of thing Rockstar or Take-Two are interested in repeating, especially when legacy movie studios are in the decline and they’re the entertainment industry’s latest massive shots.

It has been revealed that good afternoon from Washington, where Party Animals has not forgotten the 5 a.m. wake-up required last Tuesday to attend Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s first Pentagon press conference in six months. This was a peculiar one, arranged so Hegseth could brief the public on his own personal battle for career survival.

The briefing kicked off at 8 a.m., but the press had to be at the Pentagon by 6 a.m. for an extensive security screening. I’d like to think that this cruel early start was a consequence of Hegseth’s self-proclaimed sobriety. What kind of drunk drags his sorry carcass before a crowd of jackals before noon? Not any I know.

But sources I spoke with for a latest piece on Hegseth’s war inside the Pentagon told me there was a more Machiavellian motivation for the presser: Donald Trump loves to watch Fox & Friends at 8 a.m. And sure enough, soon after the conclusion of Hegseth’s performance, its intended audience of one offered a review on Truth Social.

Read on for my investigation into Hegseth’s turbulent tenure at the top of the Department of Defense, and what it means for his survival as Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Recent findings suggest that the reviews are in for Joe Biden’s fresh book, Promise Me, America. The Atlantic calls the book “unrepentant.” The New York Times calls it a 400-page “cover letter.” The former president offers the fantastical opinion that he should have stayed in the race in 2024 and faced Trump, quite a position to maintain given he couldn’t voice his own audiobook and limited his press appearances for the release to a soft-focus People magazine story (his publisher did not respond to Party Animals’ multiple requests for an interview). According to the reviews, the former president dedicates scant attention to one of the biggest debacles of his presidency, the war in Gaza, which he abetted thanks to near-unwavering support for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as 2,000-pound bombs rained down on the densely packed enclave, killing more than 70,000 people. As president, Biden publicly questioned the death toll numbers. “Too many innocent Palestinians were killed,” he now writes, as if possessed by the passive-voice ghost of Donald Rumsfeld. Mistakes were made, indeed. Meanwhile, 31 former employees have been fighting Rockstar in court over claims they were fired as part of union-busting tactics, which the company denies. All of this makes a silly Call of Duty parody commercial in GTA 6 far more interesting, as the ad directly references unionizing and its benefits.

Sources indicate that in GTA 6, you can find many radio stations playing hundreds of songs. But these stations also have DJs and commercials, including ads for in-universe movies, books, indicates, and even video games. One of these ads is for the newly introduced AAA military shooter Righteous Slaughter: Domestic Infection, the latest entry in the GTA universe’s satirical spin on Call of Duty. The ad claims the biggest threat to the country is a disease that makes people think “anti-American thoughts.” One sign someone has been infected with the “Liberal Cuck Contagion”? They start thinking about fair wages and unions.

Towards the end of the ad, two soldiers fighting to stop the disease have this exchange:.

Soldier 1: “You know, we’ve been working on this mission with no benefits, no security…”.

Soldier 2: “What are you saying??”.

Soldier 1: “Maybe we should look into… unionizing?”.

Industry observers note that soldier 2: “They got Jimmy! I repeat, Jimmy’s infected!!!”.

You can hear the full ad below:.

In a vacuum, it’s a funny skewering of how military shooters tend to be more conservative in their politics, often presenting soldiers as heroes of American values and the way these same right-wing folks often hate concepts, like unions, that improve people’s lives.

But in the context of the ongoing union recognition vote and court battle in the UK over Rockstar’s firing of 31 employees who were involved in union activities at the studio, this joke hits differently. It almost feels subversive, like the people who helped write and produce this ad in GTA 6 are punching back at their own bosses and the folks at the very top of Rockstar Games and parent tech giant Take-Two Interactive. Right now, both sides are awaiting the judge’s ruling.Â.

Sources indicate that “With a recognised union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to,” wrote Rockstar developer and union member Nestor Uriarte in The Guardian recently. “Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too.”.

According to recent reports, “Whatever happens in this ballot, our union will continue fighting for a studio that works for every single person at Rockstar, and for workers across the industry. Unionising shouldnât be something we simply admire from afar when dockers, miners or teachers do it. Itâs something we can, and must, embrace for ourselves. The future of the industry shouldnât be a game played over our heads.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Minor spoilers ahead for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.
  • It has been revealed that the Hunger Games movies (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription) have entertained audiences for over ten years, and we've got yet another book to screen adaptation in theaters now thanks to Francis Lawrence's Sunrise on the Reaping film.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Minor spoilers ahead for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

It has been revealed that the Hunger Games movies (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription) have entertained audiences for over ten years, and we've got yet another book to screen adaptation in theaters now thanks to Francis Lawrence's Sunrise on the Reaping film. My favorite scene from the book was unfortunately cut from the prequel movie, and I had to ask both the director and actress Mckenna Grace about it.

In a recent development, I loved the Sunrise on the Reaping book, and was wildly impressed by how well it was adapted for film. Unfortunately, the scene where Maysilee kills a Gamemaker alongside District 4 career Maritte didn't make it. As you can see in the video above, I asked Francis Lawrence about this decision, where he confirmed the sequence was shot during principal photography. In his words:.

In a recent development, it's probably the most debated sequence that we had throughout the development process. What happens is, because of that action with the game makers and because of the fight that happens with Maysilee and Haymitch after, it was a fight that in the book is about implicit submission. And the argument that some of us had was that he was already no longer submitting. Like, you know, if you've been down to Sub A, if you've done the things that he's done without spoiler in this movie he's not submitting anymore. And so it didn't feel like it thematically fit.

It has been revealed that points were made. While it would have been awesome to see Maysilee kill a Gamemaker, in the novel it's connected to her relationship with Haymitch. They have an argument afterward about him still implicitly submitting to The Capitol, and not killing the Gamemakers despite being the closest Tribute to them. As director Francis Lawrence told me, that confrontation between the District 12 tributes didn't make sense for the movie adaptation, especially after following Joseph Zada's protagonist as he attempted to break The Arena.

This sequence was indeed shot, so the debate about whether or not to include it in Sunrise on the Reaping extended to the post-production phase. As the director went on to tell me:.

We shot it. We even augmented the fight to be, tried to be about different things. And then that thematically didn't fit. And so we ended up cutting it from the movie, but I believe will be one of the deleted scenes that will be available.

Industry observers note that fingers crossed that we get to see this scene sometime in the future, via special features when the latest Hunger Games prequel is released to homes. This isn't the only change made to Sunrise on the Reaping, which included some references to Lucy Gray Baird from Songbirds and Snakes. Of course, I had to ask the actress who brought Maysilee to life about the cut sequence.

While interviewing the cast of the newly introduced Hunger Games movie, I asked Mckenna Grace about Maysilee's cut scene. She spoke about the argument with Joseph Zada's Haymitch that followed the Gamemaker death, telling me:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, that argument scene was one of my favorite things that I got to do because it was just Joe and I in the woods like screaming at each other. I think that what it was, was it didn't make sense for our characters to be split at that time because we didn't have enough time to repair it like they did in the book. And we didn't have the scene, you know, where they're splitting the sardines like in the book. And so it just didn't make, it didn't make sense for them to be so split at that time whenever their bond had just become so strong. Because they didn't get to reforge it and go and burn through the hedge together.

Points were made. As awesome as it would have been to see Maysilee kill a Gamemaker with one of her poisoned darts, that sequence also complicated her relationship with Haymitch shortly before her death. Instead, Francis Lawrence and company decided to keep the District 12 tributes as a united force until Mckenna Grace's character was killed by bird mutts. As such, the death and Haymitch's reaction are given extra emotional weight.

Adapting novels for film is a tough task, and there's always some content that ends up on the cutting room floor. Recent findings suggest that latest arrivals are landing in the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, but at the same time, you can also expect a few departures from that gaming library. Fortunately, the number of games leaving soon are on the smaller side, as there'll be only three exits in total. Unfortunately, one of those games that you're running out of time to play through the Game Catalog is a massive and pretty fun fantasy title, so get those hours in while you can. PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon Granblue Fantasy Relink Granblue Fantasy Relink Somerville Fade to Silence This month's biggest departure is Granblue Fantasy Relink, a massive fantasy game with a storybook art style, cinematic boss fights, and a large roster of characters who all possess unique abilities to master. First released in February 2024, Granblue Fantasy Relink is built around real-time combat and flashy team-up mechanics, making for a visually striking experience overall. While the story isn't much to write home about, it's the gameplay and worldbuilding where this Granblue spin-off shines, and it got even better earlier this year with the Endless Ragnarok expansion. In comparison, Somerville is a story-rich puzzle game that's oozing atmosphere with its slick art direction, and Fade to Silence is a single-player and co-op survival-crafting adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world that is feeling the chill of an eternal winter. While the Game Catalog is going to be a little poorer without those three titles, it is getting some great games this month. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is the headline act, and it'll be joined by several more titles like Atomfall, Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake, and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii. All PlayStation Plus subscribers can also grab a trio of freebies between now and November 30: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered, and Monster Train 2.

If you're having trouble accessing certain Apple products and services today, you are not alone. As of early Tuesday afternoon, Downdetector reveals user reports of concerns across multiple Apple services. While Apple's System Status page initially revealed far fewer issues than Downdetector consumers reported, the site has since updated to reflect general outages.

In a recent development, according to Apple, the disruptions aren't quite as widespread: Apple states that the App Store, Apple Music, AppleCare on Devices, and Schoolwork are all experiencing outages. Apple says that the App Store and Apple Music "may be slow or unavailable," while AppleCare purchase is presently unavailable. The company's System Status page indicates an "issue" with iCloud Account & Sign In. Other services with user reports on Downdetector, including the Apple Card, Apple Online Store, and Apple Business, read as "Available." Apple also says there was an outage with the Volume Purchase Program, but that has since been resolved.

Recent findings suggest that it's not clear what's causing the issues with the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud Account & Sign In, or other Apple services at this time. However, the timing is odd. It comes after a number of banks experienced outages on Monday, as well as Microsoft's massive outage the previous week. In addition to all of these outages, the FAA unexpectedly grounded all U.S. flights on Friday, for only the third time in the agency's history.
